walkthroughs.body_html: The Tanakh's three parts are Torah, Nevi'im (Joshua to Malachi) and Ketuvim (Psalms, Proverbs, Job and later writings). The acronym Tanakh comes from the initials of these sections. The Masoretic text became the authoritative version.

Rabbinic tradition holds that an Oral Torah accompanied the written Torah from Sinai. The Mishnah systematised oral teachings around 200 CE; the Gemara expanded on it, producing the Jerusalem (c. 400 CE) and Babylonian (c. 500 CE) Talmuds. The Babylonian Talmud became dominant.

Daf Yomi, completing the Babylonian Talmud over 7.5 years, illustrates the ongoing centrality of study. Midrash and later medieval commentators like Rashi continue to inform reading. Modern movements interpret tradition variously: Orthodox, Conservative/Masorti, Reform/Progressive and Reconstructionist.
